questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,\,{v}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,uv⟩$ at the point where $u=0$ and $v=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=0$ and $v=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(0,2) & =⟨2,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(0,2) & =⟨1,\,2(2),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,4,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(0,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(0,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,\,2,\,7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=0$ and $v=2$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2(0)+2,\,{2}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,0\cdot 2)=(2,4,0),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-8,\,2,\,7⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-4,\,z⟩ & =0 \\ (-8)\cdot (x-2)+2\cdot (y-4)+7\cdot z & =0 \\ -8x+2y+7z+8 & =0 \\ 8x-2y-7z & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given Some Parameter Values
questions.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩$ at the point where $u=\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{3},\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}_{v}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -\sqrt{3} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{3} & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{3} & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-2\sqrt{3},\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{2}$ correspond to the point 

$$
(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}))=(1,\sqrt{3},0),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2,\,-2\sqrt{3},\,0⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-\sqrt{3},\,z⟩ & =0 \\ (-2)\cdot (x-1)-2\sqrt{3}\cdot (y-\sqrt{3})+0\cdot z & =0 \\ -2x-2\sqrt{3\,}y+8 & =0 \\ -x-\sqrt{3}\,y+4 & =0 \\ x+\sqrt{3}\,y & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Plane to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
questions.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=1-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,y=-v,\,z=-u
$$

at the point $(-1,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨1-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,-v,\,-u⟩.
$$

First, notice that since $(-1,-1,1)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}=-1 \\ -v=-1 \\ -u=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=-1 \\ v=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2v,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=-1$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(-1,1) & =⟨-2(-1),\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(-1,1) & =⟨-2(1),\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(-1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(-1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,\,2,\,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y+1\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ (-1)\cdot (x+1)+2\cdot (y+1)+(-2)\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -x+2y-2z+3 & =0 \\ x-2y+2z & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x=2{u}^{3},\,y=u{v}^{2},\,z=v
$$

at the point $(2,9,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2{u}^{3},\,u{v}^{2},\,v⟩.
$$

First, notice that since $(2,9,3)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{u}^{3}=2 \\ u{v}^{2}=9 \\ v=3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=3.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2{u}^{3}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2uv,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨6(1)^{2},\,{3}^{2},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,9,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) & =⟨0,\,2(1)(3),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,3)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,3) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 6 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨9,\,-6,\,36⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨9,\,-6,\,36⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-9,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ 9\cdot (x-2)+(-6)\cdot (y-9)+36\cdot (z-3) & =0 \\ 9x-6y+36z-72 & =0 \\ 3x-2y+12z & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Normal Vector to a Parametric Surface Given a Point on the Surface
questions.problem: Compute a normal vector to the parametric surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨v,\,1+u,\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}⟩$ at the point $(1,2,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $(1,2,1)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}v=1 \\ 1+u=2 \\ {u}^{2}{v}^{2}=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2u{v}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2{u}^{2}v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨0,\,1,\,2(1)(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨1,\,0,\,2(1)^{2}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,2,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
